findings.title: Guidance as practicable direction
findings.claim: The focus guidance and course carriers meet the later acts of release, feeding, and care for a near person, so the shown routes become directions enacted for another person.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries both showing the right way and an intended course; the supplied 90:13-16 sequence gives those routes concrete objects and needs. The contact changes guidance from information received into direction embodied in freeing, sustaining, and drawing near.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the two shown ways as routes with practical consequences, not only as knowledge placed before a human being.
findings.containment: The later acts remain contextual triggers for an additive reading. The focus clause still plainly says that the human was shown two ways; this finding does not make every later act a lexical gloss of the verb.

epistemic.reason: The citable cross-run record is trusted and its two focus branches are directly supported; the supplied same-surah connection rows provide the wider act sequence.
